request: 文字を入力したらレインボーなQRコードが派手なアニメーションとともに表示される

spec.name: rainbowqr
spec.summary: rainbowqr shows the given text as a QR code in the terminal with a rainbow color animation.

flags.name: d
flags.help: animation length in seconds (0 disables the animation)

behavior: B1: Text is the single positional argument if one is given; otherwise all of stdin is read. Trailing \r and \n characters are removed from the text. More than one positional argument prints 'rainbowqr: too many arguments' to stderr and exits 2.
B2: If the text is empty after trimming (empty argument, empty stdin, or only newlines), print 'rainbowqr: no text given' to stderr, then the usage line, and exit 2.
B3: If -d is negative or NaN, print 'rainbowqr: invalid duration' to stderr and exit 2. Invalid flag syntax also exits 2 (standard flag package).

B4: The QR code is made with qrcode.New(text, qrcode.Medium) from github.com/skip2/go-qrcode. If this fails (for example text too long), print 'rainbowqr: ' followed by the error message to stderr and exit 1.

B5: If stdout is not a terminal (checked with go-isatty) or -d is 0, no animation and no escape codes are used: print qr.ToSmallString(false) to stdout unchanged (lines of space, ▀, ▄, █ characters), and exit 0.

B6: If stdout is a terminal and -d > 0: hide the cursor, then draw frames at about 30 ms intervals for -d seconds. Each frame draws the QR bitmap (qr.Bitmap(), including its quiet-zone border) two rows per text line using the half-block characters, with 24-bit foreground colors (ESC[38;2;R;G;Bm) whose hue depends on (column + row) and the frame number, so the rainbow scrolls. In the first half of the duration a sweep reveals the QR from left to right (columns not yet reached are blank); the sweep front is drawn in white. Frames after the first move the cursor up to overwrite the previous frame.

B7: The last frame is fully revealed with the rainbow colors. After it, reset colors (ESC[0m), show the cursor again, and exit 0, leaving the final QR on screen. The cursor is also restored on error paths after hiding it.
B8: Nothing is written to stdout other than the QR output; the program does not read keys and does not use the alternate screen.
